To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT (not circulated yet) — Handover for the launch, Thursday 26 November

DRAFT — written by Marieke on the train tonight. Please do not circulate until I have read it back over.

THE ONE-MINUTE VERSION
Figure 3 uses the wrong 2030 revenue number. The correct figure is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The paper PDF is already fixed; the deck (slides 6 and 9) and the embargoed press release are not. The press release has to be corrected and re-issued before Wednesday's journalist calls, because 34 journalists already have the wrong number in their inbox. Everything else follows from that. The findings of the paper do not change — this is a correction to one headline figure, not a change of conclusion.

FIRST, THE THINGS I WANT YOU TO KNOW
Inês, I found the error on Monday afternoon and I am leaving you with it. That is not fair and I am sorry. The mistake is mine: I carried the 2030 estimate from the old run into the deck and the release and did not check it against the final run. If anyone asks — a journalist, Kessler, anyone at all — the error was mine, it was found and corrected on Monday, before publication, and the correction is already with the right people. Say it plainly and do not let anyone put it on you.

I trust you completely with this. You know this paper better than I do, you ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself, and you are much better live than you think you are. When the projector died at the COP side event in Lisbon you held the whole panel together and nobody in the room noticed a thing had gone wrong. You do not need me there to hold it together, and I am not going to pretend otherwise. Take the seat, take the calls, take the decisions.

One personal thing and then I leave it alone: my father is ill, I am with my family. If it comes up, that is the whole of it — there is nothing more to add.

On logistics: I am travelling tonight and I will be largely unreachable tomorrow morning, so I may reply late and might not pick up after 9. You can call me whenever — but please do not wait for me. If something needs deciding, decide it and tell me afterwards. Nothing below depends on me.

WHAT IS ALREADY DONE (so you do not redo it)
- Paper PDF v7 is corrected (pages 3, 14 and 15) and is the version to quote from and to print.
- Deck v4 is 14 slides with my speaker notes still in it (written for 20 minutes — see step 5).
- Abena Owusu-Mensah's remote link is in the calendar invite and she tested it; it works.
- Room booked by Lindqvist's office, badges collected by Tomás, light lunch from 12:00 outside the room.
- The embargoed release went out Friday to 34 Brussels contacts, embargo until Thursday 10:00.

WHAT STILL NEEDS DOING, IN THIS ORDER

Step 1 — Fix the number in the deck (tonight or first thing tomorrow).
Slide 6 and slide 9 both carry the 2.1 figure. Slide 9 is the revenue chart: redraw it from the final run with 1.4 billion for 2030 LDC-relevant revenue, or lift the corrected chart from PDF v7 page 14. Slide 6 is text or a callout with the number in it. Grep the whole deck for "2.1" and for any other "billion" values that came from the old run.

Step 2 — Correct the press release and re-issue it under the same embargo (Wednesday morning at the latest, ideally Tuesday).
Hanna should send an updated version (v2) to the same 34 contacts, clearly marked "corrected version, 25 November", with a short note: the 2030 LDC-relevant revenue figure is EUR 1.4 billion, not 2.1; this was an error in the earlier version, found and corrected before publication; the paper's conclusions are unchanged. Do not let the correction wait until after Wednesday's calls — if a journalist quotes 2.1 on the record at 14:00 on Wednesday, we are managing a story instead of a figure. If Hanna wants a senior name on the correction, Geert can sign it off; just ask him, he knows the situation.

Step 3 — Check for other copies of the wrong number (Wednesday morning).
Web teaser, the one-page summary, the newsletter scheduled for Thursday, anything already scheduled on social. I do not think there are many, but one stale 2.1 on a website on the morning of the launch is the kind of thing that follows us all week.

Step 4 — Names for security, to Tomás by Wednesday 12:00 sharp.
He is firm: without final names by Wednesday 12:00, security will not let our guests in. From our side I expect Inês Carvalho, Lucy Tran and Lucy's colleague (I do not have her name — can you ask Lucy directly? I would rather not guess). Add Hanna if she is coming. Abena is remote, no badge.

Step 5 — Cut the presentation to 15 minutes.
My 20-minute version no longer fits: the panel now starts at 12:50 and Lindqvist has to leave at 13:30. Your slot is 12:35–12:50. You have 14 slides and my speaker notes; the notes are written for 20 minutes, so roughly a third has to go. You know this paper and you know which slides carry the argument — you do not need my slide order, only the one hard constraint: 15 minutes, and slides 6 and 9 corrected. Put your own voice in it rather than reading my notes; they were written for me, not for you.

Step 6 — Work out who moderates after 13:30 (decide by Wednesday, not in the room).
Lindqvist moderates and wants to take at least two questions herself before she leaves. That leaves 13:30–14:00 without a moderator. Ask Tomás whether her office will nominate someone or whether she expects you to take over; if nobody is named, you take it. Abena is good at holding a panel remotely and can cover it if the connection is solid.

Step 7 — Wednesday's calls at 14:00 and 15:00 (Hanna to confirm the format).
I was meant to take those. My suggestion: you take both, with Hanna on the line, since you can speak to the annex B numbers without notes. The trade newsletter call is likely to be technical; the Belgian daily more likely to want the story. Both lines you need:
- "The 2030 LDC-relevant revenue figure is EUR 1.4 billion. An earlier version of our release carried 2.1; we found it ourselves on Monday and corrected it before publication. The paper's conclusions are unchanged."
- If asked why 2.1 ever appeared: "It was an error in the earlier draft, from an earlier modelling run. We corrected it before the launch." Do not go further than that and do not try to reconstruct the old run for a journalist.

Step 8 — Thursday, the day itself.
10:00 embargo lifts (corrected release goes out). 12:00 guests at the security entrance, badges from Tomás. 12:30 welcome from Lindqvist, five minutes. 12:35–12:50 your presentation. 12:50 panel: Abena (remote), Kessler, you. Lindqvist moderates and takes at least two questions before 13:30. Q&A continues, close at 14:00. Light lunch outside the room from 12:00. I have asked Tomás to update the run of show, which still says 20 minutes and a 12:55 panel — if he has not, correct it so the room and the panel are working to the same times.

THE PANEL AND KESSLER
He wrote to us before the event about the 80% pass-through assumption, and he will open on it and try to make the launch a debate about steel users' margins rather than about the paper. Do not let him set the frame. Two things help:
- Open your answers with the corrected headline and the central case, then treat pass-through as what it is: the central assumption in the paper, with a sensitivity range. Say it openly — "80% is our central case, which is why annex B runs 40% and 60%." That is not defensive; it is our own robustness check. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Both of those numbers are yours, so you can say them without checking anything.
- On resource shuffling: we agree it is a risk. Section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission set it out in its monitoring report. Say that plainly and move on.

If you are asked directly who made the 2.1 error, the answer is that it was mine, that we found it on Monday and corrected it before publication, and that nothing in the paper changes. Do not get drawn into a longer account of how it happened.

PRACTICAL LIST
- Print a few copies of PDF v7 and have the corrected deck on a USB stick and on your laptop, plus the PDF as backup. In Lisbon the room let us down; do not depend on the room wifi or the house adapter.
- Test Abena's link on Thursday morning from the room if there is time, and have her mobile number to hand.
- Lucy Tran needs two photos and the attendance numbers for the Halvorsen grant report by 4 December. Take the photos yourself, or ask the office to be there with a camera, and do not let Thursday slip past you on this.
- Anything outside the paper and the event goes to Hanna; anything that needs a senior name or a sign-off goes to Geert.

CONTACTS
Hanna Weber — press release, embargo, media calls. Geert Lammens — senior sign-off on the corrected release. Tomás Reyes (Lindqvist's office) — timings, badges, moderation hand-over, room. Lucy Tran — attendee name, photos, attendance numbers.

I know this is a mess to hand over at short notice and that the error is mine. Thank you for picking it up. I will answer messages as soon as I can, and I am sorry to be leaving the room to you.

Marieke
